headline: Medium risk: shared API-driven workflows can create output-trust and resource-conflict issues, but no direct shared-channel or secret-handling pathway is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between argo-workflows and ComfyUI: argo-workflows exposes REST/GRPC and ComfyUI exposes a Comfy API, but neither profile shows clipboard, MCP, stdin/stdout, or filesystem bridging. Without a bridge, prompt injection into one cannot reliably steer the other.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies ComfyUI outputs into Argo workflow parameters without sanitization, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate networks or namespaces.
Do not pipe model text into workflow definitions.
Require explicit human review before promoting generated text into commands.
Add provenance labels to any transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content filtering at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch non-secret operational data classes, and ComfyUI can read model files while argo-workflows handles artifacts/parameters. However, neither profile requests secrets or shows shared workspace access, so leakage is not evidenced by default; uncertainty stays low because the pairwise data path is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, file leakage becomes plausible.
IF either agent is configured to ingest arbitrary local files, sensitive artifacts could flow across the boundary.
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and storage buckets.
Mount only the minimum required directories.
Disable any optional file-import features not needed for the task.
Rotate or redact sensitive artifacts before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo-workflows can call REST/GRPC APIs and ComfyUI can run multiple instances only if configured externally, but ComfyUI explicitly reports no filesystem write, git, shell, or subprocess capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the remaining risk is limited to API-level contention, which is small in the documented setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable API-backed resource, request contention can occur.
IF an external orchestrator serializes access, the conflict is reduced further.
mitigations: Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Assign distinct output directories or API namespaces.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workflow object.
Use idempotent operations where possible.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo-workflows can consume artifacts and parameters, and ComfyUI produces workflow-related outputs; if Argo treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad generation can cascade into downstream automation. The profiles do not show verification gates by default, so the interaction exists in default API-driven use even though the exact handoff is undocumented.
conditions: IF Argo uses ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as workflow inputs without validation, errors can propagate.
IF downstream steps trigger deployments or notifications, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between generation and execution.
Require schema checks on all transferred outputs.
Keep human approval before any irreversible action.
Log and diff generated inputs before use.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no secrets handling, regulated-data claims, or residency constraints, so no concrete compliance breach is evidenced. The only relevant compliance surface is generic artifact/workflow handling in argo-workflows and media/model handling in ComfyUI, which does not by itself establish a mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, a separate policy review is required.
IF one deployment is subject to residency or retention rules, the pair must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems.
Document retention for artifacts and generated media.
Review deployment region settings before use.
Restrict logs to non-sensitive metadata.
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware data routing.
